text: One thing you must remember. Is that the Gita is the first, the most ancient of the scriptures which have examined this question of how to approach the truth. This is the first scripture to declare that there are different paths to the supreme being. Each chapter of the Gita is a description of a different path. Nowhere in the Gita is it said that this path is better than this path or the other path is worse than the other or anything of that kind. They are all different approaches. Meant for different kinds of people, depending on their Gunas.
author: Sri M

text: Intellect is essential but intellect has its limitations – it cannot take us to the inner. When we have to go to the core of our consciousness, we have to keep all these thoughts at bay. Keep them away and go deep within and try to find out. Nothing should be allowed to intrude. A great master said, ‘When you leave your shoes out there, when you come in to meditate, leave your personality there and come. When you go back, you have to function in the world, so put them back again!’
author: Sri M

text: ‘From the unreal feeling or from the unreal understanding or unreal imagination, that I am the body, may I be lifted to a plane where I may begin to understand that I am the Reality. May the reality dawn on me so that I realize that I am the immortal Self and not the body.’
author: Sri M

text: If you think of one thought at a time, when one thought is gone, before the other comes, there is something. If it is not thought, it has to be something else. That something else is the consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: If you read from any of the Upanishads and commentaries of Shankara and others, you find what they are trying to say is that while the intellect is a very powerful and useful weapon for us I mean an instrument for us. The highest function of the intellect is to understand its limitations in the spiritual field.
author: Sri M

text: The few who with their great devotion and good deeds who become recipients of divine grace, free themselves from likes and dislikes, the opposites of attachment and aversion, and with their purified intellects see the impermanence of mundane existence, sorrow, old age and death realizing that the only blissful, permanent, reality is the Supreme Being, meditate on the Supreme Being in the inner-most depths of their consciousness and attain the Blissful goal of eternal spiritual fulfillment.
author: Sri M

text: When I am clear, when I have not a single thought touching my mind, when I can control what thought I want, that is not fantasizing. Fantasizing automatically means replacing reality with something unreal. Here you are touching the essence of reality.
author: Sri M

text: For a spiritual search, you need not belong to any particular section. It is an individual, personal affair. There is no need to be affiliated to anything – but be free from it. As far as spiritual search is concerned, it is an individual, personal effort. Nobody becomes spiritual en masse. En masse thousands of people cannot suddenly become spiritual. It is an evolution.
author: Sri M

text: The path which has been described by all the important teachers, unfortunately, happens to be narrow – not because of any narrowness in thinking but because the other paths are so wide and inviting that it is very easy to go off on those paths – they are all highways. This may be a small little path going up – a pugdandi raasta.
author: Sri M

text: According to the Vedantic teaching or according to what Ramana Maharishi said….who was, I think, one of the latest contemporary teachers of Vedanta who had the experience of it. He said that when you pursue this ‘trying to find out who you are’, then you begin to think, ‘Maybe I am the mind.’ Then you say ‘Yeah, I must be the mind’ – then ‘Whose mind?’ and so on.
author: Sri M

text: How many people search for the Truth? Very few. Actually, in the Bhagvad Gita there is a beautiful statement. Krishna says, ‘Among millions of people one turns to the spiritual path. Among millions of people who turn one walks the path and attains it’….that is very rare, it is not easy.
author: Sri M

text: We have not changed. You see – the way of doing things has been polished and perfected. That’s what intellectual life has taken us to. There are other good things – we have found medicines for diseases; but we haven’t found medicines for the disease of ignorance. And the disease of misery – That nobody has found yet.
author: Sri M

text: However much we may try …because the brain is a very limited organism and we get limited inputs. All that the brain can think of and decide and conclude is from the information that it gets – the inputs. Now the inputs themselves are limited because the sensory organs that gather the inputs themselves are limited. Therefore any information, any understanding that the brain, has is limited. It cannot be unlimited. And we are seeking the unlimited.
author: Sri M

text: Now, from the point of view of spiritual evolution, the greatest duty of an intelligent human being is to find the Truth. And, religions have made the duties of a human being so that we may stay together as a society. Very often, when you go on the path, you might have to go alone – alone, like a lonely traveler.
author: Sri M

text: Prasna Upanishad is an Upanishad which questions and does not accept but questions before accepting. And that should be the hallmark of all enquiries. Not believe because somebody said so, but question. Ask!
author: Sri M

text: I look at this world and I see, through ordinary common sense, that it is not permanent. It is not permanent, it is temporary and what is temporary cannot be real. Everything is getting destroyed. In fact, a part of our lives is spent in trying to rescue that which is getting destroyed and protect it.
author: Sri M

text: Arjuna asks “Among those who worship the unmanifest and those who worship you as the manifest as Krishna, who is a better yogi? Krishna says, does not answer that question directly, he says: “as long as one has one’s mind fixed intently on me, on me meaning The Truth (here), in steadfast love and with absolute faith.” So if that(absolute faith) can be there then that yogi is superior, means absolute attention, faith and steadfast love of the supreme truth. If that is there no matter whether it is manifest or un-manifest that Yogi I consider to be (superior).
author: Sri M

text: Dedicate all actions. (then) Slowly, the outside disappears and the inner takes over. Whatever happens – good or bad – that it is the Lord who does! And whatever you enjoy – think that it is the Lord who is enjoying. Gradually one will be able to free oneself from the worldly traps and go within. But usually what happens is when you say we have surrendered to the Lord, everything is done by him – usually it is only the bad things that we say “Why has God done this to us?” Anything that is good we like to take credit for (ourself).
author: Sri M

text: There is an ancient sloka which is chanted before starting various activities. Sahanavavatu – we have chanted it many times, it is interesting to learning meaning of it – sahanaubhunattu sahaviryam karavavivahe. Tejas vinavaditam astu, maa vidveshavahai. Which means, both the teacher and the one who is listening – are as important. May both of us be protected. May both of us be nourished. May both our vitalities increase. May our ‘tejas’ – the fire of understanding – increase. Then the last sentence is very very important. Let us not fight among each other. Let us not quarrel with each other. Because we are not trying to argue or prove our point. What we are trying to do is sit together and try to understand a problem. Which are two different things. That is a dialog.
author: Sri M

text: Very often, we tend to mistake tamas – tamo guna – for sattva. Sattva is goodness and calmness and quietness. Tamo guna is not goodness and calmness and quietness but laziness, sloth and pretending to be good.
author: Sri M

text: From my personal experience I would say that since the ‘Truth’, is in the present, an ever living experience, and not anything that can be gathered and stored in memory, memory being a thing of the past – there is no present memory – all so called knowledge even the intellectual or verbal understanding of the Truth is still Apara-vidya and nothing to be proud of or gloated over.
author: Sri M

text: Again, in Gita, is an exhortation to perform action and not to run away from it. It is not that one becomes inactive. On acts but one is not caught by the results of the activity. This is karma yoga. Otherwise, suppose I decide, that the sorrow and the problems of the world are too much for me. And I run away to the Himalayas. Or somewhere else. I can’t run away from my mind. I can physically run away from my situation. But my mind follows me, wherever I go. I can’t change that. So the teaching of the Gita is, don’t run away. Because you carry your mind with you. Stay where you are. And deal with the situation.
author: Sri M

text: So, I am here today, I work hard, I think happiness comes out of a solid bank balance. I have done everything. And then, what happens? Suddenly, destiny takes someone away from me who is most dear to me. Then, I begin to wonder, whether it was worth amassing it all; now, what will I do with it when the person for whom I collected it is gone?
author: Sri M

text: The only way to study yourself, the only way to know yourself, the only way to realize yourself, to understand yourself as you are and not as you imagine you are, is by being a part of the society. Communicate, interact, so on and so forth—without prejudice, without condemning, without justifying.
author: Sri M

text: This (examination to know thyself) is possible only in the midst of society. You cannot really study your mind—that is ‘to know your Self’—in isolation. Sitting in a cave, there is no one with whom you can interact—no one to get angry with, no one to be jealous of, no one to assault in anger.
author: Sri M

text: Self-realization is to understand oneself and, in the process of understanding oneself, break down innumerable illusions that we have about ourselves.
author: Sri M

text: ‘The taught’ is listening and the teacher is teaching and a stage comes when they so intimately understand each other that the ‘taught’ becomes the teacher. One who is taught becomes the teacher because his mind and the mind of the teacher have become One, there is no division between the two. That comes only with a great deal of work, a great deal of exercise, mind exercise; exercise of one’s thought process.
author: Sri M

text: We all know we are the body. Slowly, we start thinking and we begin to realise that I cannot be the body because the body belongs to me and what belongs to me cannot be me….this is not me. Now it is me, now it is not. So, this is my body….then what am I? Who am I? Then one proceeds looking into this question carefully and one pursues it.
author: Sri M

text: It is by itself a contradiction for the limited to seek the unlimited. When the limited understands its limitations; that is intelligence. That’s all, it need not be intellect. When the limited understands its limitations and then says this is not way the way to find it, it becomes quiet. It is only then, there is hope that the other will make itself known.
author: Sri M

text: Every one of us, although we say we are looking for this or that, is looking for philosophy or welfare. What we are really looking for is happiness.
author: Sri M

text: Kundalini is considered by the tantras as the manifestation in the human being of the infinite supreme energy. This energy called Parashakthi or Bhavani is said to reside in potent form, not kinetic, not active but an inactive form at the base of the spinal cord, of all human beings – coiled like a spring. In the tantric symbology it is shown as a snake turned three and a half times around itself and waiting to be awakened by the spiritual practitioner.
author: Sri M

text: The Tandav Nritya of Shiva is meant to free you from all conditioning, all images, all attractions and repulsions that keep you rooted to the understanding that you are an individual different, and not the same as everybody else. So if you are ready to embrace the dancing Shiva, then you are free, if you are not, then you are not!
author: Sri M

text: Look inside our minds and we will see that we have hundreds of images and it is because of these images that we get hurt, our ego goes up, we have all the problems, everything! I believe that I am an intelligent man, now somebody pricks it by telling me I am a bloody fool, I am terribly upset. Why? Because I have created an image that I am an intelligent man.
author: Sri M

text: True consciousness means to go beyond all images – not images that you see around you – but the images that we build up in our minds and the Tandav nritya is a beautiful expression of the breaking down of all the images that we have created. So many images!
author: Sri M

text: They say Adinath dances his Tandav Nritya. When he dances his Tandav Nritya, he destroys images. He explodes all the images that we have created and nothing new can come up. Like death destroys the old, the stratified, the calcified and the fossilized!
author: Sri M

text: When the mind churns in meditation which means, when you delve deeper and deeper into the layers of your mind, the first thing that comes out is not Amrit. The first thing that comes out is poison because, that’s the only way it can come out and disappear, which is why many people who start the practice of sadhana, after a while give up sadhana and take on to other things because the poison has come out.
author: Sri M

text: Shivarathri, traditionally, is supposed to be the day when Samudra Manthan was done and the poison came out. You know that story of the churning of the ocean-the Manthan- and when the churning took place, first a very powerful poison called ‘halahala visha’ is supposed to have come out and it would have enveloped the world but for the fact that Shiva is supposed to have drunk it up. It stopped in his throat so it became blue, so He is called Neelkant. This is a fact which is applicable to all yogis, not only to Shiva.
author: Sri M

text: Every practitioner of spiritual exercise should keep in mind -that when you practice and go deeper and deeper, all the tendencies that have been hidden in your subconscious mind till now-bottled up – they will all come to the surface. That is the poison. That is where you might get some help from a teacher, who knows how to handle it, otherwise, everything can go berserk.
author: Sri M

text: Suppose I decide that the sorrow and the problems of the world are too much for me, and I run away to the Himalayas or somewhere else, I still can’t run away from my mind. I can physically run away from my situation. But my mind follows me, wherever I go. I can’t change that. So the teaching of the Gita is, don’t run away because you carry your mind with you. Stay where you are and deal with the situation.
author: Sri M

text: If one understands that one is not the body but the inner self which is consciousness, then one begins to understand how to deal with sorrow. But unless and until some kind of sorrow comes, one does not realize the unreality of existence and wake up from it. Sorrow shakes one up. Happiness is some kind of a chloroform. It anesthetizes and puts one to sleep. It is like having one peg too many. You wake up in the morning with a hangover.
author: Sri M

text: Most of the activities of the world that we perform, based on the assumption that we are the body, bind us down to the earth. Karma Yoga is the theory or teaching which says, that if you can act knowing well that you are actually the supreme ever free self and not the body, then none of these activities can bind you down to sorrow.
author: Sri M

text: The highest function of the intelligence, according to the Upanishads is to realise its limitations and when it realises its limitations it just keeps quiet. It knows, ‘I’m very useful in this and that, but I’m not very useful here.’ So, the ‘I’ has to just pipe-down. When the ‘I’ pipe-down then ‘the other’ Is.
author: Sri M

text: Those who have transcended the external rites of religion, they should begin to look within to find the true essence. This is very essential because without the true essence, sometime or the other, the external will collapse and that is not a good thing for the world. Religion is essential but religion should be practiced sensibly, by not being insensitive to others.
author: Sri M

text: Freedom is our birth right. Our true self, the atman is free; it does not need to be freed from anything. It is free because it is complete, ‘poorna’. ‘Poornamadah’ that completeness is actually you in your true essence. ‘Tat tvam asi’ You are that! Realise O human being, Realise O man that you are eternally free. Never have you been conditioned, never have you been bound. It’s all in the mind that you are bound or conditioned.
author: Sri M

text: Praying is a beautiful psychological exercise where you deep down want to come out of the circumstances which are limiting your progress. And not finding that in the present conditioned mind, try to appeal to the higher mind to bring about a breakthrough. Through it you can reach what normally cannot be reached, that is prayer.
author: Sri M

text: Most of the time we spend all our energies on worrying about failure. If we could only just brush it out and retain our energies – we could move forward and look at fresher avenues. A mind which is insecure and confused, cannot think clearly. And when one is in a state of what is called – depression, it is to avoid this kind of thing that the Gita talks about Karma Sanyasa Yoga. Means perform your Karma, and forget about the result.
author: Sri M

text: Actually, if you are a practitioner of yoga or sadhana, your attention becomes very, very good. You are able to concentrate fully on whatever activity that you are doing. If your complete concentration is on the work that you do – then nine times out of ten, it will turn out to be good. Suppose it doesn’t; You have no control over it. Then why worry about it? Brush it aside and move forward. This is Karma Sanyasa Yoga.
author: Sri M

text: I am saying if that desire or intense desire to be free of suffering arises in a human mind, that mind need not be an extraordinary intellectual or any such thing. It can be just an ordinary person but that intensity of desire to get out of it is mainly emotional, not intellectual. When that emotion comes, when that feeling comes, then one can completely direct oneself towards the way by which one can be free.
author: Sri M

text: The root sorrow is the wrong identity. One thinks one is the body. And being body oriented, one gets all the sorrows. One experiences sorrows because anything that happens to the body and anything in relationship with other bodies – is the cause of sorrow.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t think that the spiritual teacher should be like this….if he’s not like this, then he is not a spiritual teacher. This is not true because there may be many reasons for which a spiritual Master may be acting in a certain way, which you realize only by moving with the person. Therefore, it is very important to move with the teacher for some time. ‘Move with the teacher’ meaning ‘to live with the teacher’ at least for some time, interact with him / her to find these things out.
author: Sri M

text: The best thing is – better than not doing your duties is to do your duties. But don’t neglect your spiritual journey; keep that up seriously, so that when you are mature enough, you are out of it. Even if you don’t want to, you will be out! That is nature’s law! So, as long as that maturity does not come, it is a good idea to stay at home and do your duties.
author: Sri M

text: There is this great Buddhist chant of the Mahayanas, which says, ‘At some point or the other, in our endless cycle of rebirths, every individual on this earth must have been our mother! Therefore I bow before all the individuals on this earth; help me to take them to Nirvana.’
author: Sri M

text: Naama Smarana is one of the easiest and the best – you don’t even need to ask anybody to do Naama Smarana. Along with that you should also take care of other aspects of one’s life, little disciplines that one should follow. And for that one need not go into details, but the most important root discipline from which other things come is less for the self and more for the others. This is the way to the spiritual field.
author: Sri M

text: Can our ‘sundowner’ be the name of God? Can we have that special whisky that is not available even in Scotland? Can we listen to that music which moves our hearts and opens the doors to extra sensory perceptions? I am not talking about powers. We are saying there are centers in the human system, other than the ones used by the ordinary human mind to solve its day to day material problems.
author: Sri M

text: The secret of visualization – creative thought – is to actually believe and visualize picture details, what one wants, to be as if one is already there. When this is done, the subconscious mind carries it to the higher level, which we could call the super-conscious mind. When the mind is open, and when there is the great desire to achieve something then the channels for achieving it are opened.
author: Sri M

text: Amrita need not necessarily mean nectar which you drink. It need not mean something that excites the taste buds. Amrita comes from the word ‘a – mrita’ which means immortal or deathless. Amrita – that which confers deathlessness upon a person. Again it does not mean physical deathlessness. All the great sages have come and gone. Nobody remains forever. But the realization that there is something in us that is immortal and which survives the body.
author: Sri M

text: The first thing that happens as one advances in sadhana is that one develops compassion in the heart. Therefore, some people (who) do not even believe in God, there are such people... but they feel for others so much that they are ready to sacrifice their lives for them. Such people according to the 12th chapter of the Gita – Bhakti Yoga – are nearer to Krishna, than others who always say, ‘Krishna Krishna’.
author: Sri M

text: The word ‘Upanishad’ is that which is learnt sitting close to the teacher with complete humility to understand the ultimate supreme truth. So the Gita itself is said to be an Upanishad. What is the content of the Upanishad? Brahma Vidya - knowledge or understanding of the Brahman, the supreme reality behind all phenomena that we see, the supreme reality which is in you and me and which pervades the entire universe. The understanding of that is known as Brahma Vidya.
author: Sri M

text: The Northern (upward) movement of the Prana is when it finally goes through the seven wheels or the seven psychic centres along the sushumna nadi until it reaches the highest heaven in the Sahasraara chakra, full of water. The water here means apastatva, the tatva of liquidity, of movement identified with the moon or the Soma. Having reached there, the Rishi is never unborn and he lives identified with the omniscient.
author: Sri M

text: Matter which is non-living, inanimate matter and the anima – the life which animates it – Prana has produced all that you see on Earth! The sun indeed is life. Why? Because it is the sun that causes photosynthesis, it is the sun that makes life. If the sun stops working for some days, there will be no agriculture, no growth, nothing! It is the sun that gives light and heat. The prana or life energy, in the form of the light of the sun, bathes the entire Universe in its four directions, with life.
author: Sri M

text: Moving up and down the spine is Mukhya Prana, the Supreme energy. In yogic terms, it is the movement of the aspiration, thought, concentration and energy towards (either) the higher side or the lower side. When it goes down it leads to material wellbeing. When it goes up, it leads to Spiritual wellbeing.
author: Sri M

text: If you have faith in an infinite supreme being, put all your heart into what you want to do or achieve. Pray hard, that is very simple, anybody can do it but pray with great feeling. The emotions and feelings help to keep our goal properly fixed in the fulfillment circuit. And when it is switched on, there is no blockage, it goes straight up. So pray. Pray in the morning, pray in the evening, pray whenever you want. Pray not only for yourself but pray for others. Even the very fact that you keep praying for something records the desire in you, stronger and stronger in your mind until the desire turns into a reality.
author: Sri M

text: If you can put your mind into an idea which you want to achieve, with complete visualization as if it is actually there, not as you want it, but as if it is actually there; if you can do this constantly and if you know a technique by which that can be done, believe it or not, sooner or later, it becomes a reality.
author: Sri M

text: You see, it is very simple. When we are little infants, we are helpless.. Even if we have to go to the other room – somebody has to lift us and put us there. We can’t even go to the toilet. Somebody has to take us there. We can’t eat. Somebody has to feed us. During the end too, when we become old and helpless and fall sick – again the same thing happens. In between, there is a period, when we really think or imagine that we are under control. Actually, we are not under control. If we realize this, then we have surrendered.
author: Sri M

text: In the Gita, the chapter after Arjuna Vishada Yoga is Sankhya Yoga, the Yoga of knowledge. So, seeing that Arjuna is in sorrow, and observing the miserable state he has gone into, Krishna explains to him and begins the teaching of the knowledge required to handle this sorrow.
author: Sri M

text: When the sleeping energy – the great Kundalini is awakened by resorting to proper means, guided by a proper teacher, it awakens and begins to move up the Sushumna channel, touching six centers as it ascends. It reaches the topmost center, known as the thousand petalled lotus – the Sahasraara Chakra which is actually located at the crown of the head and when the energy reaches there, it merges with the supreme reality called – Shivam. When both merge, the Yogi enters Samadhi or a high super conscious state where he realizes his own identity merges with that divine, all pervading supremely blissful being.
author: Sri M

text: All these activities like blood circulation and so on are not under our control, breathing too. We don’t say, ‘Breathe!’ And therefore the lungs breathe. It goes on by itself. But we can also voluntarily control it to an extent, not breathe for a few moments or breathe slowly and so on. That is one activity which we have some control over. Therefore it is a direct link to that which controls all our activities.
author: Sri M

text: When Patanjali in the yoga sutras defines yoga, he defines it as yogas chitta vritti nirodha. This means, yoga is the stopping or the stilling of the vrittis of the chitta. Chitta means mind stuff – thoughts. We all know that, when we say mind it is a collection of thoughts. You cannot conceive of a mind without thought.
author: Sri M

text: My master (Babaji) once talked about how three people went to Himalayas to meditate. They went up the snow clad Himalayas, sat down with closed eyes and meditated. After one year, one of them opened his eyes and said, ‘It is quite cold here’. Then he shut his eyes and went back into meditation. Another year passed. The second man opened his eyes, and said, ‘I think you are right’, then closed his eyes and went back into meditation. Then at end of the third year, the third man opens his eyes and says, ‘why don’t you two guys just shut up and meditate?’
author: Sri M

text: The limbic system is that which takes care of our feelings. If the limbic system didn’t work we would have no feelings. Therefore, in the raising or awakening of the Kundalini, emotion or feeling plays as much part as the technique of pranayama and the chanting of the mantras. According to the tantriks, any feeling which is very deep can in some way awaken the kundalini.
author: Sri M

text: The crescent moon is a symbol of Shakti. You see it in Durga and Kali. The Navadurgas all have a crescent. Crescent is also the last digit of the moon either when it is waning or waxing. The crescent – therefore – is considered to be the sixteenth letter of the sixteen lettered Sri Vidya.
author: Sri M

text: You think you are this little pool of stagnant water that stands on the way with no movement whatsoever. The Guru says “Look my dear fellow you are a lion, you are not a goat. You are not this little pond of stagnant dirty water that stands there, you are the ocean. So don’t live under the illusion that you are the limited. You are the unlimited”!
author: Sri M

text: The yogis say that the joining or the crossing together, the sangam of the Varuna and the Asi rivers are in the human body, the ida and pingala at the brumadhya. This is called the ajna chakra situated in the center between the eyebrows. This is the holy city of Varanasi, the meeting place of the Varuna and the Asi rivers.
author: Sri M

text: Those of us who do pious acts, charity, sacrifice themselves for others thinking that is the work one should do, really win the human world! But, they are not free of desire and, therefore, they return again, reborn. Their lives have not ended; they come again.
author: Sri M

text: This crescent moon is also called Soma. Therefore Shiva is called Somashekhara- one who keeps or retains Soma. Soma has two meanings. One – is the moon, you have the physical moon. The other is, the imagination – (it) is always associated with the moon.
author: Sri M

text: We can go anywhere but we carry our mind with us. We can’t escape from the mind. So, the only way, according to the Gita and also according to people who have walked on this path at least to some extent, is to face it, examine it, look at it and handle it. It’s only then you get over it.
author: Sri M

text: You see, it is very simple. When we are little infants, we are helpless.. Even if we have to go to the other room – somebody has to lift us and put us there. We can’t even go to the toilet. Somebody has to take us there. We can’t eat. Somebody has to feed us. During the end too, when we become old and helpless and fall sick – again the same thing happens. In between, there is a period, when we really think or imagine that we are under control. Actually, we are not under control. If we realize this, then we have surrendered.
author: Sri M

text: The first Chakra – the mooladhara – represents prakrithi, the solid earth or solidity. The next one – the swadisthana, which is silvery and which is shaped or symbolized by the crescent moon – represents the watery tatva or the aapa tatva, also called the ‘tejasa’ or the dream tatva.
author: Sri M

text: If the mind is made up of thoughts and thoughts are always vibrating, moving - sometimes up, sometimes down, constantly in motion; that movement of thought or the waves of thoughts are known as vrittis. The stopping of the vrittis – that complete stopping of the movement of the vrittis, is considered to be yoga or Yogas Chitta Vritti Nirodha.
author: Sri M

text: So what I’m saying is that irrespective of whether you are an intellectual or what normally can be called a non-intellectual, irrespective of this condition, the most important condition to find the truth is an intense desire. This, of course is emotional too.
author: Sri M

text: Praying is a beautiful psychological exercise where you deep down want to come out of the circumstances which are limiting your progress. And not finding that in the present conditioned mind, try to appeal to the higher mind to bring about a breakthrough. Through it you can reach what normally cannot be reached, that is prayer.
author: Sri M

text: Therefore the importance of bhajans, kirtan , going to places where other people worship and going on pilgrimages, all lead you to the stimulation of the emotional parts of your minds, for opening up centers that you can experience.
author: Sri M

text: The salient feature of the last chapter (Bhagavat Gita) – the 18th Chapter – is after saying all this, and taking Arjuna through the whole course, the last chapter Krishna says, surrender everything unto me. I will take care of your moksha. That is the sum and substance of the statement which means, ultimately one realizes which Arjuna also realizes – that this is not intellectual acrobatics.
author: Sri M

text: Arjuna attempted to run away from it and hide. Krishna says, ‘Face it! There is no way you can get rid of it. Face it. Understand the reason for it. If you understand the reason for it, then you can be free of it forever.’ And the reasons that Krishna makes him understand (are) in the Gita. It is also for us to understand.
author: Sri M

text: The next chapter (after Karma Yoga) is called, Karma Sanyasa Yoga, where Krishna says that sanyasa is not giving up activity but not getting caught up by the results of the activity. Let go and Rejoice! Tena Taktyena Bhunjita which means you do your work, but don’t get caught up with the results of the act. If it is good – fine. If t is not good – also fine.
author: Sri M

text: To discover that unconditional ever free self in all human beings was the aim of the spiritual teaching in ancient India. Break free from all bondage, all psychological bondage, realize that your true self is ever free and never bound! This was the clarion call of the great and ancient Upanishadic teaching - Moksha, moksha, moksha !
author: Sri M

text: Vedanta is not intellectual acrobatics. You can stand on your head. You can study all the scriptures. You can know them by heart. But, unless and until, the quality of mind improves, one cannot find the truth. And how does it improve? By understanding that one (is not in control).
author: Sri M

text: According to the tantras, Shiva – the Supreme Being – resides on the Sahasraara Chakra, with his legs let down and touching the brumadhya or the center between the eyebrows. The point at which the sushumna enters the Sahasraara Chakra is known in the tantras, as the ‘Bramharandra’. It means the hole or the gateway to Brahman, the Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: The theory of tantra is that the sexual energy which you know, for all human beings after food and shelter – is the most enjoyable experience. It is that same energy – the sexual energy – which is sublimated to travel up in the upward direction, instead of the downward direction.
author: Sri M

text: Is there unbound freedom? That was the quest of the Upanishads. And the Upanishads said YES, there is such a freedom. They said, they also experienced it I am sure that the true self of the human being, the true self of a man or a woman, the essence of one’s being called the consciousness in its absolute purity is free anyway!
author: Sri M

text: When one has discovered one’s true freedom, is it irreversible? I think, the question need not be asked. Once you have realized your freedom, when you have realized that you have ever been free, how can it be reversed?
author: Sri M

text: At the end of the 18th chapter, Krishna declares now that you have understood everything, relax. Let go and rejoice! Do your things. Carry on. Nothing is going to happen. The roof is not going to fall on your head. Proceed in the path.
author: Sri M

text: In our ‘Parampara’- the Nath Parampara- the first Guru, the first teacher is supposed to be Adinath and Adinath is none other than Shiva. Shiva and Adinath are indistinguishable. The most important sadhana here is to worship the Guru, look at Him, meditate upon Him, and also follow the teachings that He has given; the most important of which is to consider all living beings as part of yourself, because, if you don’t have that, then all this worshipping is no use.
author: Sri M

text: A spiritual teacher teaches a person sadhana according to that person’s capacity and according to that person’s needs. Everybody cannot practice the same thing. Why? Because nobody is made the same way. Some people may have a devotional temperament, some intellectual, some maybe practioners of yoga – there are different kinds of people, and accordingly, one has to teach.
author: Sri M

text: Self-realization to me, Kaivalya or Moksha, means not free from something, but realizing that one is always free but has been labouring under the illusion that one is not. Yes, this is the same as ultimate freedom, the freedom from which one never falls back to non-freedom or bondage.
author: Sri M

text: Imagination or Visualization is a divine capacity given to the human mind by which it can visualize and make reality out of its visualizations. This is because it derives its capacity to create from its true essence which is the Atman.
author: Sri M

text: A snake has been the symbol of Kundalini for many 100 years. It is also because it is the symbol of wisdom. It is a symbol that you find on the head dress of pharaoh for instance, or in the legends of the Nagas who are supposed to be snake gods and therefore representing wisdom.
author: Sri M

text: A person who has touched that freedom, a person who has understood this freedom, moksha or mukti, this completeness, lives an unprejudiced life of total freedom not influenced by the stereotyped images that one encounters in day to day life.
author: Sri M

text: The word Guru has a deeper meaning, it means the capacity to initiate the process in others, to enquire and investigate into the meaning of what the world is and what is our relationship with the world and also existence of a deeper level of consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: In India, in Ancient India, the young aspirant, the neophyte, the brahmachari went to the masters, the Rishis, seeking not wealth, not health, not position, but pure and unconditioned freedom. And this pure, unconditioned, unbound freedom is called moksha or mukti.
author: Sri M

text: Sai Baba was very fond of remembering and singing God’s name. He always uttered, “Allah Malik hai” and in his presence made the others sing God’s name, bhajans and kirtans continuously, day and night, for all 7 days of the week – the naam saptaha!
author: Sri M

text: A person who has touched that freedom, a person who has understood this freedom, moksha or mukti, this completeness, lives an unprejudiced life of total freedom not influenced by the stereotyped images that one encounters in day to day life.
author: Sri M

text: You cannot practice attaining freedom in day to day life. Freedom is not something that you practice; it’s something that you attain. It’s something which is you, which is yourself. You can’t practice it.
author: Sri M

text: The important aim of the Gita is to lead one to the main character in this whole drama of life, this whole kurukshetra of life, Krishna, the supreme being. Krishna not as a human being, not as the form but as the consciousness that animates everything that exists in this universe.
author: Sri M

text: They speak of him as father as the FATHER. That being – having five feet and twelve forms seated in the higher half of the heavens, full of water and then again others speak of him as the omniscient sitting on a chariot of seven wheels and six spokes. Now this needs quite a bit of explanation! Seven wheels and six spokes are all expressions that indicate the psychic system of the Nadis which exist in the human body.
author: Sri M

text: The sun, is a symbol of the Supreme primordial life energy, the Vaisvaanara which pervades all objects, protects all objects, gives life to everything on Earth. The poet, the Rishi is also known as the Kavi, praises that Supreme Being!
author: Sri M

text: The ecstasy that one experiences when the sexual energies are gathered together and made to awaken the Kundalini, and when that kundalini reaches the Sahasraara chakra at the crown of the head, it is a multiple orgasm that no human being experiences anywhere below in any of the lower centers.
author: Sri M

text: It is interesting to note that the Bramharandra – if you compare with present day anatomy – sort of coincides with what is known as the center of the limbic system, where the pituitary gland, the amygdala, the thalamus and so on, exists in the brain. Almost the center of the brain!
author: Sri M

text: Let’s say the guide, the teacher, or friend who has crossed to the other side, who has learnt to swim and cross the ocean of samsara, such a teacher who is our true friend, what does he do? He teaches you how to swim so that you can cross the ocean.
author: Sri M

text: Practice austerity, chastity and stick to the truth. Be chaste, be pure and have faith that the answer will come after you have lived thus. So, that is the preliminary preparation for the understanding of the truth. This we are not prepared to do and yet want to find the truth.
author: Sri M

text: I can know many things but if I don’t act on it then it makes no sense either to me, or to others. So the third chapter (after Sankhya Yoga, the yoga of knowledge), is Karmya Yoga which is, to act on the knowledge you have received so far so that you grow, evolve and move on to the next step.
author: Sri M

text: Philosophically, Buddha for instance, talked about freedom from sorrow for all mankind which he defined as nirvana which is another word for moksha. According to the Buddha, desire is the root of all sorrow and freedom from desire is freedom from sorrow for all mankind.
author: Sri M

text: I’m trying to draw a line between intelligence and intellect. Intellectual is gathering more and more information. Intelligence is to do with understanding. Intellectuals are those who gather knowledge from all sources.
author: Sri M

text: I do not say that humans are born with intrinsic freedom. I say that the true self of every human being is eternally free; and when I say eternally free, it’s free even before birth. At birth, it is in fact slightly conditioned.
author: Sri M

text: This is a very, very serious question. Is a Guru necessary to attain freedom? Does the Guru induce freedom? If the Guru is inducing freedom, it cannot be freedom. It can only be something similar to freedom.
author: Sri M

text: Reality is not that things don’t exist but they don’t exist in the form or state in which we think they do. That wrong understanding of objects, of anything is called Maya, a misunderstanding. And that is the great illusion.
author: Sri M

text: The rising of the kundalini therefore is the rising of consciousness from the gross to the subtle, subtler and subtler levels until It reaches the highest stage in the sahasraara chakra and the yogi enters into a deep trance which is an altered state of consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: Even in the smallest of selves bound by chains, a human being experiences true freedom for he or she realizes that one has never been bound. This is the immortal great message of the Upanishads.
author: Sri M

text: Imagination or Visualization is a divine capacity given to the human mind by which it can visualize and make reality out of its visualizations. This is because it derives its capacity to create from its true essence which is the Atman.
author: Sri M

text: Vaisvaanara is the Lord who has all forms, the golden one, the Sun, the all knowing, the goal of all soul-light, the giver of heat possessing thousands of rays existing in hundreds of forms. Thus rises the Sun, the life of all creation.
author: Sri M

text: Very often, we tend to mistake tamas – tamo guna – for sattva. Sattva is goodness and calmness and quietness. Tamo guna is not goodness and calmness and quietness but laziness, sloth and pretending to be good.
author: Sri M

text: Sa Esa Vaisvaanaro Visvarupah. This is HE, the Vaisvaanara fire, assuming every form, life and fire that rises everyday, this is declared in the verse of the Rig Veda.
author: Sri M

text: You cannot practice freedom because freedom has no design, it has no pattern. It’s absolutely free, unbound, boundless! One cannot ‘practice’ freedom in day to day life.
author: Sri M

text: Surya, the life of all creation, the golden one, the all knowing, the goal of all soul-light, the giver of heat, possessing a thousand rays, exists in hundreds of forms, which means there is only ONE reality, the essence of the Supreme.
author: Sri M

text: When one has reached the Sun – the spiritual Sun that is eternal and fearless – one does not have to come back into this world of sorrow. That is the final goal.
author: Sri M

text: Now Vaisvaanara is supposed to be the fire, which is the essence of living beings, the life, the prana, the energy that glows in all human beings, while Visvarupah is the essence of the whole Universe.
author: Sri M

text: Remember that in this particular field that is the spiritual journey, sometimes two plus two may be nine, and not four. Because we are entering quantum land where nothing is certain.
author: Sri M

text: According to Vedanta that feeling of being dependent on what is around you, the feeling that you are bound and that you have to get out of it, is part of the great illusion of the mind called the Maya.
author: Sri M

text: Does this freedom happen in stages? I would say, It’s like the wheel; the network of illusion is gradually lifted as one goes deeper and deeper into understanding one’s own self, one’s own mind.
author: Sri M

text: From ancient times, meditation has been defined as one-pointedness, where the mind is not allowed to be scattered or dissipated in different directions. In fact, if you learn the art of being one pointed in meditation or in day to day life, you are automatically in a meditative state all the time. If you are one pointed in your day to day life, you are one pointed in meditation too. It is not possible to be one pointed only while meditating.
author: Sri M

text: The highest function of the intellect is to understand its limitations in the spiritual field. This is possible only if you have really good intelligence; good intelligence sharpened by concentration and one-pointed attention that is free from distractions of the world.
author: Sri M

text: Mantra is a technique and not the goal. When you feel you have entered a deep state and chanting the mantra also takes effort, Stop! But watch out, the mind is very tricky, it may be laziness which may be preventing you from chanting. So, examine carefully.
author: Sri M

text: Praying is a beautiful psychological exercise where deep down, you want to come out of circumstances that are limiting your progress. Finding that the mind with its present conditioned capacity is not able to do it, you are trying to appeal to the higher mind to bring about a breakthrough. A prayer is to reach out to that which normally cannot be touched.
author: Sri M

text: The centre which is at the navel is known as the ‘manipura’ chakra. When the heat of the practice of kundalini yoga emanates from the manipura chakra, then the kundalini rises further up, from solid to liquid and from liquid to the gaseous state passing through the center of the manipura chakra.
author: Sri M

text: The anahatha chakra is also called the anahath, because when the mind is fixed on this center, one hears the sound which is unstruck. This means the inner sound, which is the sound of ‘Om’ or pranava. It vibrates within this chakra when the mind or consciousness ascends to it.
author: Sri M

text: All things about spiritual matters boil down to your relationships, day to day. We can sit at home and meditate for hours but when we come out and we are still the same, it does not work.
author: Sri M

text: Kamadeva, once went to Shiva and tried to shoot his arrows of desire on Him. Shiva, the mighty lord of the yogis, who had conquered all desire and who was supreme and peaceful, is supposed to have just opened his third eye – which is the eye of knowledge, and Kamadeva was burnt to ashes in no time.
author: Sri M

text: There is a story in Shiva Purana about Kamadeva – the god of love. Kama actually can best be translated as desire, could be any desire – sensuous, non sensuous. Kamadeva, shoots arrows of flowers at us, and even the Gods can fall under his power.
author: Sri M

text: When the third eye or the center, which is known as the agna chakra is activated or opened when the kundalini energy reaches the ajna chakra, then the mind understands the reality behind all illusion. Then all illusions are burnt to ashes.
author: Sri M

text: Once all illusions are burnt to ashes, one arrives at supreme satisfaction, unlimited bliss and happiness. Therefore one has no other desire left. This happens when the Kundalini reaches the ajna chakra, which is the last but one step towards Moksha.
author: Sri M

text: The more something is done for oneself only, one can say it is wrong. The more something is done for others and of that, a little bit is for oneself, then I can say it is the right way. That is the only distinction I can make between right and wrong.
author: Sri M

text: Alchemistry is actually the metaphoric expression of purifying the mind, of the soul. The base metal which is the gross mind can be purified and made very subtle and pure. Then the same mind turns to gold.
author: Sri M

text: Shraddha - people say it’s faith but I would translate shraddha to total one-pointed attention. Saburi is patience. Patience is essential because when all are swimming along the stream and allowing ourselves to be carried away in one direction, one person in a million is changing direction and is trying to swim against the stream, so it is not easy. There is no other way than to have infinite patience.
author: Sri M

text: If we can voluntarily extricate ourselves from the conditioning thoughts that are in our minds and open up for receiving what is beyond the three dimensional world and the ordinary way of thinking, perhaps we can tap the infinite potential that is even now, waiting for us inside our own minds.
author: Sri M

text: The whole science of meditation is a way to go beyond or go deeper than the surface of the mind, explore the deeper recesses and come up with greater abilities and greater understanding. So much so that the mind realizes compared to what it was accustomed to, it has almost reached infinite heights
author: Sri M

text: Great yogis, great rishis, great scientists, the ‘great’ in all fields, are those who are not satisfied believing the conditioning of the mind. They know that this is basically a prejudice and try hard to break through, come out of their shell and soar to great heights in whichever field they are involved in.
author: Sri M

text: Intelligence has to realize that from a point, it’s function is over and allow something else to take over. That instrument of perception that takes over is known as intuition, Jnana Drishti. You will see Shiva meditating with eyes closed and one small eye drawn in the centre of the forehead. That eye is the eye of perception of the highest and goes beyond the function of the ordinary brain.
author: Sri M

text: My Master used to say. “When you sit down to meditate, if you have someone you don’t like, think of that person standing before you. Bow down to that person mentally and say that you are a spark of the Divine; I have nothing against you; you are God himself in this form – bow down first and after that, begin your meditation.
author: Sri M

text: When you enter the meditation hall, leave your shoes outside along with your ego; don’t bring it in. Go inside like a new-born child who is free, you have no enemies, you don’t hate anybody, at least for the time being. This is easier said than done but it’s the easiest way to bring about a completely tranquil and deep meditative mind.
author: Sri M

text: In self-defense in Kalaripayattu they say, ‘never do anything when you are angry’ because all your calculations may go wrong. So let your anger go, cool down, and then perform your action.
author: Sri M

text: Babaji used to say, ‘The seeds have been planted, they have been sown but no seed will become a tree and bear fruit in three days, it takes its own time’. So sow the seed, keep the climate clear, water it properly and then we’ll see what happens.
author: Sri M

text: Krishna says - You should be able to control your senses. You should learn to cultivate tranquility and balance of mind in any situation, good or bad; and above all, have the welfare of all living beings in your heart. These are the qualifications required. It doesn’t matter how you worship God, whether you think of him as with form or without form.
author: Sri M

text: One of the meanings of Upa is to move closer to the Truth, Ni means to sit at a lower level than a teacher and shad means to sit down. When I sit down to study with my teacher, I sit down with the awareness that I do not know, therefore, let me understand. It doesn’t mean physically lower. The moment I say I know then all my inquiry stops. I cannot hear anything because I shut my ears with the feeling that I know. Again, I may hear but interpret it according to what I already know. This is also a dangerous thing.
author: Sri M

text: When I enjoy something sweet, fresh jalebis for example, although the enjoyment wells up when my tongue touches the jalebi, it is not in the jalebi or the tongue, it’s in me; a certain enjoyment wells up within me. The yogic theory is that the source of all enjoyment, the reservoir of all happiness is within us, the spark of the divine called Sat-Chit-Ananda.
author: Sri M

text: Upanishad means that which is taught by the teacher to the student through which he moves closer to The Truth. Upanishad is not in the words, it is in what is transferred between the teacher and the student.
author: Sri M

text: Remove all the conditions that are there and remain in that One essential state. This is the aim of the Vedantic teaching. One discovers that one is not this body nor the mind but the inner self, the atman which is free of all unhappiness and which by essential nature is Sat Chit Ananda, or true happiness.
author: Sri M

text: The practice of yoga is the way of finding that happiness which is our true identity. We discover that we are not what we think we are, but something entirely different. Swami Vivekananda explained it beautifully. He said, “We are hypnotised by the false happiness that the world seems to give us. We have to de-hypnotise ourselves and come back to our senses.
author: Sri M

text: Let Go! The Upanishads have a beautiful saying “Tena tyaktena bhunjitha” – Let go and rejoice! Normally when you say rejoice, we have ideas of accumulating things. Here it is a completely reverse process - Let go and rejoice! It doesn’t mean you should sell everything you possess and go away. That is not the meaning. ‘Let go’ means you let go of all the things of the past and stay in the present.
author: Sri M

text: Krishna says that if you would only fix your attention on ‘me’; He speaks not as a human being but as the manifestation of the Supreme Being. ‘If you fix your attention on me with complete faith and absolute attention and great love, then I will certainly save you from the ocean of birth and death.’
author: Sri M

text: Don’t unnecessarily complicate life with too many things. Speak the truth; More than speaking the truth, think the truth. That does not mean that when you speak the truth you have to be blunt. There are sweet ways of speaking the truth. You need not be brusque and then suffer because of that.
author: Sri M

text: The agni tattva, vis-a-vis the mind is actually the fire that burns within. Physically it is the digestive fire. It is the fire, the aspiration to transform oneself from crude to subtle. Agni ye swaha.., it means, ‘May agni purify my mind and take it from the concrete to the less concrete, to the subtle’.
author: Sri M

text: You have a slate and you write on it. Every time you write on it, if you want to write anything else, you have to rub it off. Otherwise you can neither read it, nor is there space to write anything more. So in matters of inner exploration, the most important thing is to keep your slate clean
author: Sri M

text: Pranayama – usually when we say pranayama people think it has something to do with either slow or fast breathing or something to do with the breath. Actually the word pranayama means the knowledge or the rules regarding prana, the life energies.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t carry your anger and hatred, stupidity and poisonous feelings against others from one day to the next. When we go to sleep, can we leave it there and get up fresh in the morning and say, ‘That’s okay. Yesterday is over’.
author: Sri M

text: The Bhagavat says that wherever there is a manifestation of goodness, energy, power, position, status and knowledge – especially knowledge, that is automatically a manifestation of the Supreme Being. But it may be an amsha, a part and may not be a poorna avatara. It is an amsha avatara of the Supreme.
author: Sri M

text: Each of the chakras starting from the mooladhara to the sahasraara have their associated sounds known as the bijaksharas – seed sounds. When the yogi fixes his attention on a chakra and continuously chants the bijakshara, the energy is supposed to activate or awaken.
author: Sri M

text: The Soundarya Lahiri, the Lalita Sahasranama and other tantric texts contain certain bijaksharas or seed sounds that actually have no meaning by themselves but are vibrations that awaken the Kundalini and make it move up the spine till it reaches the sahasraara chakra and unites with the Supreme Lord.
author: Sri M

text: Human becomes divine, man becomes superman and the ordinary is transformed to the extraordinary by the magic touch of the supreme energy. When the atman merges with the supreme paramatman, when finite happiness is replaced by infinite bliss known as ‘anantham anandam’, the unending happiness of the soul is soaked in the bliss of the supreme meeting between Siva and Shakthi. This is celebrated so well in the Soundarya Lahiri of Adi Shankaracharya.
author: Sri M

text: Fixing the attention – one pointed attention either on an idea, an object, on a sound, on a thought or even an idol but one pointed with no other thought intruding is called dharana.
author: Sri M

text: Instead of trying to be free from the beginning, enjoy with the purpose that you want to be free of it ultimately. How does one do this, by dedicating everything to the Supreme Being. Whenever you enjoy, keep in mind that the actual enjoyer is the Supreme Reality or the spark of the Supreme Reality which is in me.
author: Sri M

text: ‘Yogo bhoga yatey‘– yoga through bhoga. Again this is not a license for bhoga, bhoga means enjoyment. What the rishis meant was while you enjoy, realize that the enjoyment is not coming from that object you enjoy but it is tapping a little bit of happiness from the inner source, the reservoir of all happiness. Gradually you become independent of all external objects, go to the root of enjoyment and begin to enjoy within; then you are free.
author: Sri M

text: We are all in some activity or the other, nobody can remain without doing anything; The Lord says, ‘Dedicate that to me. Think that I am the agent and I am the enjoyer’. Gradually you will get purified enough and be lifted out of that activity. Although this is the primary, the beginning and elementary form of spiritual development, it is applicable to most people.
author: Sri M

text: The Lord says, ‘If it is difficult for you to serve and purify yourself to the state of attaining the capacity to meditate, simply surrender yourself to me. Your mind is automatically controlled. Give up the fruits of all your actions. Work, but surrender the fruits to me because I am the agent and I am the enjoyer.’
author: Sri M

text: Samadhi is when you are meditating upon the Supreme Being and there is no individual meditator but only the Supreme Being. In the sankhya parlance, the atman merges with the paramatman. In Vedantic language, the atman’s identity has disappeared and only the paramatman or Brahman remains. In the language of the bhakta – he is so lost in contemplation of God that he forgets himself, so there is only that God or Supreme Being!
author: Sri M

text: If the world were a complete obstruction to the attainment of spiritual fulfillment, the Supreme Lord would not have created it at all. The very fact that the world exists around us and also in us in our minds means, there is a function for it. It is there to make us understand, learn, grow and become complete so that when we depart from this world, or even while we are still in this world, we have evolved to higher levels of spiritual consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: The result of dharana and dhyana is samadhi. Samadhi is an altered state of consciousness wherein a person who meditates upon whatever he is meditating upon, merges with the object of meditation. There is no separate meditator and that which is meditated upon. Everything becomes One.
author: Sri M

text: In spiritual matters, you start with the understanding that there is something beyond the ordinary mind. And it cannot be known through study. Soaking in the atmosphere in places where the rishis have meditated which are great centers of energy, is the closest you can get. In these places, you just need to keep quiet and not let the mind interfere – that’s all! Just sit quiet.
author: Sri M

text: It is possible to live in this world and reach one’s spiritual fulfillment at the same time, provided, we know the rules and regulations and the traffic signals to watch out for; where we can overspeed, where we cannot, the speed limit for travelling in this world and so on. Then, we can use this world as a finishing school to graduate into the higher realms of consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: It is possible for someone to lead a life like a normal human being in the material world and at the same time keep the spiritual aspirations intact, and work in a way as to attain the aim of spiritual fulfillment.
author: Sri M

text: At places like Badri and Kedar, it is best to spend time in meditation and japa. The best Satsang is to do meditation and japa, visit temples or go to holy places. It’s not a very good idea to speak in these places. But the brain still asks questions; so we have to try and answer them intellectually.
author: Sri M

text: I personally don’t think giving up the world completely, shaving your head to renounce the world and walking away is the right way in progressing on the spiritual path. There have been examples of great saints, great rishis and great beings who have lived in the world with their families.
author: Sri M

text: Brahmacharya is the period I would say of studentship, where one spends all of his time learning, supported by others so there is no worry about sustenance. One is also a celibate as he is not married. The energy saved mentally and physically is completely focused on increasing one’s understanding and knowledge.
author: Sri M

text: After the brahmacharya period, when one has studied to the best extent possible depending on the individual’s background and capacity, one goes to the next stage called grihastha. One has a family and one works to sustain himself and his family. He continues to learn and in the end he reaches spiritual fulfillment, the ultimate aim of being on this earth.
author: Sri M

text: From grihastha, when your responsibilities are mostly wound up, you are free to spend more time in retirement in a quiet place, free from the troubles of everyday phone calls and so on, contemplating and trying to go deeper into the knowledge that you have acquired during the brahmacharya and the grihastha phases. This is called vanaprastha.
author: Sri M

text: What is that one attains in the grihastha period which is different from the brahmacharya period? Once you are married you have one more person in your life; you cannot take independent and exclusive decisions. You learn to control your emotions, control your anger and to look at the other person’s point of view.
author: Sri M

text: When you go to a cave leaving everything, you can leave the whole thing behind but remember you take your mind with you. Yes! The problem is the mind and not the materials things around you.
author: Sri M

text: My master used to say ‘When you are alone in a cave, you can say to yourself - I have controlled my emotions, I am not jealous, I am not angry!, and so on. But the fact remains – the reality is that there is nobody to get angry with and no one to be jealous of’. But things are different when you are in a family.
author: Sri M

text: I think most people who jump from brahmacharya into sanyaasa directly get into trouble after a while. They have not experienced situations that test the learning they have acquired during their brahmacharya.
author: Sri M

text: Having experienced all phases – Brahmacharya, Grihastha and Vanaprastha, one sees that nothing else matters except finding the Supreme, then one becomes a sanyaasi. A sanyaasi is one who has renounced everything else for the most precious, and discovers that he has given up mere trinkets for the real treasure! That is sanyaasa.
author: Sri M

text: The best prayer is, 'God, you know what’s in my heart; I don’t need to tell you. You are omniscient; you know everything, so do what’s best for me. This is my earnest and sincere prayer to you'.
author: Sri M

text: When you say you follow the teachings, it does not mean you can sit everyday and close your eyes for hours together - not that the mind is still - and think that you have done the job. The spiritual teaching includes looking after people, who are less privileged and who are suffering; unless you do that, I do not think that you can sit and meditate. It's not possible. Well, you can go into a hypnotic trance and think that you have gone into meditation, but you have to improve your life, you have to become less self-centered. Move outside your self.
author: Sri M

text: In this material world – earning one’s living, going through all the problems and travails of worldly, mundane existence is a necessary step in learning about spiritual consciousness and evolution to higher levels.
author: Sri M

text: Usually, the spouse is your greatest critic at home because he or she sees you in all situations. This criticism should be taken as constructive as it helps to keep one humble and vigilant, keeping watch on one’s mind as it is and not as it’s imagined to be. Unless you know your mind and yourself – as it is and as you are, there is no way you can change or transform.
author: Sri M

text: Ninety percent of the troubles in this world are caused by not talking responsibly. My Master used to say – before you speak,follow three principles. What am I going to say? Who am I going to say this to? Is this the right situation? Something maybe true, but it may not be the right thing to say in that situation. Truth, sometimes, is double-edged. It could hurt; it could cause problems. So be careful, even if one is speaking the truth.
author: Sri M

text: We need eyes to see an object. This is obvious. But we cannot see our own eyes except as a reflection in a mirror. Yet, we cannot say that the eye does not exist. It is because of the fact that the eye exists, we see things around us; similarly the ‘Atman’ or Consciousness. It is only because of this root identity that we are ‘alive’ and ‘conscious’. To realize this true identity is the main purpose of meditation.
author: Sri M

text: Generally, happiness is a rare thing because whenever I work for a particular object to satisfy my desire and I find what I seek ultimately, I want to catch it and hold on to it. The moment I get the feeling of insecurity that the object or state of happiness may slip away anytime, I become unhappy. So, the search for happiness is constant and remains unfulfilled.
author: Sri M

text: A spiritual teacher sometimes provides opportunities and situations, either deliberately or as they happen. He does not encourage people to run away from situations but to pause and remain. It is only when faced with a particular set of circumstances, one begins to realise for oneself where one stands.
author: Sri M

text: Once I examine myself and find there are things to be improved in my self – the first step is to move in the positive direction and the second, do your sadhana seriously. These are two essential steps and have to go side-by-side. One, issitting down and doing your sadhana; the other is to examine your life – see what you are and how you behave with people.
author: Sri M

text: People usually think spiritual realisation is for free. This is not true. ‘He who giveth, shall receive’. By giveth, it does not mean giving money to somebody. It is more than that. There is nothing on this earth or in heaven that can be achieved without sacrificing something – that’s why it is called a ‘sacrifice’. If you sacrifice, you receive.
author: Sri M

text: Whatever be the situations, look at them carefully and try to work out how best you can handle them. In this regard,sadhana is a significant part of your daily life. Without it, you cannot control these situations.
author: Sri M

text: We always think that only happiness is a blessing. Sorrow is a blessing too. It leads us to greater, deeper, and more permanent happiness. Sometimes, sorrow is given particularly to a person who is on the path – to see how he or she is progressing.
author: Sri M

text: It is when you are face-to-face with sorrow that you turn and look at that which is beyond. If you are forever happy sucking on your lollipop – the pleasures of the world – then nobody will look deeper into the mysteries of life, how to sort it out, or how to be free of sorrow.
author: Sri M

text: Sorrow is central. In fact, the very teaching of Buddha was freedom from sorrow for all humanity. Without sorrow, how do you get free of it? Any attempt to be free of sorrow and pain is an attempt at finding out the Truth. Every sorrow is a blessing.
author: Sri M

text: The message from ancient India has been that all humanity is one and the happiness of humanity at large is the aim of human life. ‘SarveBhavanthuSukinaha’ is an ancient Vedic dictum, which means 'The whole world should be happy'.Everywhere, as many people should be happy.
author: Sri M

text: A teacher should be a polished mirror – so that when you look, you see your actual reflection and not a distorted image. How does one change if one does not see the real picture? Look at the mirror and examine yourself – am I moving forward, am I indeed changing?
author: Sri M

text: The state where you remain alone in your true self – enjoying the bliss of your inner being – is called the ‘severance of connection with pain’. When that happens, one severs one’s connection with pain of all kinds.
author: Sri M

text: To find yourself, to examine yourself, to look at life – try and become as less selfish or ‘less self-centered’ as possible. While there is no human being who is completely ‘non self-centered’, some self will remain. Without this, we cannot function on this earth.
author: Sri M

text: Happiness is a universal search. Whether one is a believer or a non–believer, Hindu, Muslim, Christian or Sikh – everybody looks for happiness in this world. All our attempts to grasp things and hold on to themare a search for happiness.
author: Sri M

text: Navanita is the Sanskrit word for butter. So, He is called the Navanita Chor – one who steals the butter. Only by churning the milk, butter is derived. Hence, churning is essential, without which nothing can come out. And, what happens when the butter comes out? Krishna steals it and runs away. So, where are ‘You’? Nowhere. If you think on these lines even for a few minutes, you realise – for a short while – you are transported into a joyous life with nothing to worry about.
author: Sri M

text: I think all the sadhana we do is intended to mostly bring about the hunger for God – for that Truth. When that hunger has built up, then God is at your doorstep!
author: Sri M

text: Music cannot be played if the flute is filled with muck. You have to empty it out. A flute has to be hollow; you can’t blow through a solid flute! So, all the muck has to go and when it is clean, hand it over to Him. Krishna will play delightful music.
author: Sri M

text: All our lives are based upon the understanding that, 'I am the body'. The ego which is the mind is built-up based on the fact that ‘I am this body only’; but there is more to it than just the body. There are many aspects of us that are not explored.
author: Sri M

text: Whenever I think of preparing for a new day, leaving behind the old, I am reminded of the cry of John the Baptist, who declared, 'Voice of one crying in the wilderness, prepare ye, the way of the Lord! Make his path straight!' These are things we need to look into…the straight and narrow path, so difficult to walk on. The Upanishads have called it shurasyadhara – walking on the edge of a razor! And yet, it’s only by facing this and living life dangerously, that one makes momentous quantum leaps into greater dimensions – a better life, a better human being.
author: Sri M

text: Happiness is the common thing that everybody seeks. When somebody commits suicide, it is generally because one wants to escape the unhappiness, the sorrow, the sadness – hoping when one escapes from the pain, there will be some happiness.
author: Sri M

text: Once the music is heard, thenceforth our problems are solved. We are onto a different world altogether. It’s also called ‘Shabd‘. Shabd need not mean only a word– it also means a sound. That is where Krishna stands playing his flute attracting everybody towards Him, and stealing our heart along with the butter. Chitchor - one who steals the heart!
author: Sri M

text: In the language of Yoga, our flute is the spine and it is usually full of muck. Kriya is one of the ways to clean it up. One cannot do anything more; only clean it up and wait! He will sing only when He wants to. One can only wait.
author: Sri M

text: ‘Krishna’ also means all-pervading. The root is ‘Kri’, to create, an action, movement, kriya. The word ‘Krish’ means action from the core of consciousness. In fact, according to the Gnostics, the word Christ is derived from ‘Krish‘. Christ means the consciousness of divinity descended to earth.
author: Sri M

text: That Energy, That Power, That Absolute Being – which is the power in manifestation – is always Complete, and anything that is incomplete is not That. In the psychological sense – unlike individual human beings or any other limited beings – it does not have any vacuum to be filled. There are no desires to fulfill, no need for anything more to be complete. It is already ‘Purna.’
author: Sri M

text: Living in this world and experiencing life, I would say is the philosopher’s stone, which eventually can purify you from base metal to pure gold.
author: Sri M

text: No amount of bhajans or kirtans is of any use unless the heart changes, unless the heart starts to look outside oneself. If we can spend even half an hour for others, then we are moving forward.
author: Sri M

text: Examine yourself in the morning when you wake up and in the evening before you go to sleep. And see – have I changed or am I the same or worse? Am I still angry when somebody else is happy?
author: Sri M

text: When we are faced with situations, we prefer to run away from them and not meet them. Stay where you are, face your situations – how do you react with others, how do others react to you.
author: Sri M

text: The search for happiness continues. If drinking a cup of tea gives us a little happiness – then drinking it keeps us satisfied for a while. But tomorrow, we have to drink tea again to become happy!
author: Sri M

text: Don’t run away from the battle. Stay there. You cannot run anywhere. So, stay on and fight it out – but with love, affection, and understanding.
author: Sri M

text: Krishna is depicted mostly with a flute in his hand, playing beautiful music. Music penetrates the heart. It has nothing to do with the logical mind. When you listen to music in rapt attention, you go so deep that you begin to hear the inner music being played all the time.
author: Sri M

text: Krishna represents love, thus love is a comprehensive panacea for all ills. If you really understand the meaning of it – utter selflessness, not love for my own sake but love for Love’s sake – only then, it is a panacea for all problems. This is very rare. When Kabir Das wove, everyone thought he was weaving cloth. Actually, he was weaving from the warp and weft of love and devotion.
author: Sri M

text: The Energy and the Power that is manifested all over the world, right from the energy that you see in a tiny amoeba that moves, gets its food and eats it – all is Power. Now, power generates power – so the amoeba eats and gets more energy. This energy is a constantly renewing force, which is also called Para Shakti. It is the highest power!
author: Sri M

text: Nobody can say ‘I have Absolute Power’. One can say, ‘I have gone deep and touched one of the conduits of That Absolute Power.’ As long as we have the physical body and we identify ourselves with the limited, personal individual – no one can claim that one has that Power absolutely.
author: Sri M

text: The Bhagavad Gita has everything. How one has to work in the world, how to lead one's day-to-day life, how to meditate, how to be devoted, everything! It has everything!!
author: Sri M

text: The Energy and the Power that is manifested all over the world, right from the energy that you see in a tiny amoeba that moves, gets its food and eats it – all is Power. Now, power generates power – so the amoeba eats and gets more energy. This energy is a constantly renewing force, which is also called Para Shakti. It is the highest power!
author: Sri M

text: Nobody can say ‘I have Absolute Power’. One can say, ‘I have gone deep and touched one of the conduits of That Absolute Power.’ As long as we have the physical body and we identify ourselves with the limited, personal individual – no one can claim that one has that Power absolutely.
author: Sri M

text: When the so-called ‘limited’ being recognizes and realizes his inner essence, he begins to know and understand that he is not different from the Absolute
author: Sri M

text: That absolute energy, when in manifestation or movement, is called Shakti. When it is in absolute rest, it is called Shiva – here we are not talking about the personality Shankara. When it is in its potential form – absolutely at rest, without a single movement – That completeness is Shiva, the Absolute Being. And, when it moves in kinetic form, when it begins to work, then That is Shakti.
author: Sri M

text: Energy – once its work of creation, preservation, and destruction is done – still remains whole. This is not possible when we think of energy in the daily world.We work and we feel tired. We say, 'some of my energy is lost'. But here, the whole Cosmos is spun out of this energy, which keeps working tirelessly and yet remains unaltered.
author: Sri M

text: Energy – once its work of creation, preservation, and destruction is done – still remains whole. This is not possible when we think of energy in the daily world. We work and we feel tired.
