We say, 'some of my energy is lost'. But here, the whole Cosmos is spun out of this energy, which keeps working tirelessly and yet remains unaltered
author: Sri M

text: Mula’ means root and ‘adhara’ means foundation or support, the basic support. So, a rough translation would mean ‘root support’ or ‘root foundation’. This means that the energy, after doing all its work, has now settled down and that center, where it resides,is called Muladhara .
author: Sri M

text: Most traditions talk about the ‘Energy’ being raised – it has to be raised from the lower Chakras to the higher. Chakra means a ‘Centre’ – a field of Force. You cannot find a chakra or a lotus – padma , if you were to dissect a body. It is merely a field in which a certain Force operates.
author: Sri M

text: In a Chakra, the Cosmic Energy operates in ‘circles’ or ‘whirls’ at certain points of the human organism. Hence, it is called a Chakra. It is also called a padma meaning a ‘lotus’ – an ancient symbol of blooming, blossoming or something growing, slowly unfolding itself. This is how the Energy operates.
author: Sri M

text: ‘Shakti’ or Energy operates within seven centers in the human psyche. It starts with the lowest one at the end of the spine called the Muladhara Chakra, and goes up through to the other six centers, with the last one in the cerebrum called Sahasrara Chakra, the thousand-petaledlotus. The idea is that the Energy is activated from the lowest and is slowly guided up through the spine, Sushumna till it reaches the top of the head, the Sahasrara Chakra.
author: Sri M

text: The most important thing for a human being, I believe, is not to cause pain to other human beings. In the Bhagvad Gita, Chapter Twelve, ‘Bhakti Yoga’, Krishna tells Arjuna that one of the most important qualities of a devotee of mine is 'sarvabhootahiteyrataha' - compassion for all beings. Here, Krishna is not speaking as Krishna, a person, but as the manifestation of the Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: The rishis –seeing how people are constantly unhappy; seeking all the time and not getting the ultimate fulfillment – discovered that there is happiness, a complete fulfillment available to every human being. This is within oneself and is not dependent on anything outside. The search just has to be reversed to look within!
author: Sri M

text: When I eat a fruit – it’s only when the sense organ comes into contact with the fruit, that I enjoy the taste of it. But that enjoyment is not in the fruit – it is in me. I am the one who is enjoying it. The theory of Vedanta –and also experienced when practiced in life – is that all bliss and happiness lies within every living being. A little of that happiness is released when the senses come into contact with a particular object.
author: Sri M

text: Shruti means shrotrasya – ‘that which is heard’, not ‘that which is read’. So ‘hearing’ meaning ‘listening’ is an important part of the Upanishad. And, if the mind is open and clear and not comparing – and is listening carefully to what is being said, it immediately registers and you have understood what is being said.
author: Sri M

text: When all the ‘ maya ‘ or delusion has been cleared and when all the agitations of the mind are cleared, then only the true essence is left behind. What remains is complete happiness, the Truth, known as the Brahman. This is the teaching of the Upanishad.
author: Sri M

text: The meaning that Adi Shankaracharya has given for ‘ shad ’ in the word ‘Upanishad’ is ‘to shake up’ – shake the mind out of its delusion that happiness is outside and not inside. Of course in the ultimate sense, when happiness is found within, one realizes that there is no difference between inside and the outside! But the beginning has to be made inside.
author: Sri M

text: The avadhoot Dattatreya had twenty-four teachers in his life, and one of them was the honey–bee. The Avadhoot says, I learnt the lesson from the honeybee, collecting and storing for a rainy day; how it goes from flower to flower, sucks the honey and gathers it. This shows that there is nobody on this earth who knows everything!
author: Sri M

text: As long as you have a physical body, nobody can know everything. We need to learn. At any time, one should be prepared to learn. For learning deep things like the Upanishads – one needs to have the humility that I am learning something new – ‘let me listen and learn’. If I say ‘I already know’, then I cannot learn. And, in this field sometimes, all that we have studied may actually be an obstacle.
author: Sri M

text: You must have heard the famous statement that many people think is a modern English saying – 'blind leading the blind’. It is an ancient statement. It comes from the Mundaka Upanishad – ‘ andhenaiva nīyamānā yathāndhāḥ .‘ It refers to those who have learnt only theoretically and think they know– when such people lead others into spiritual matters, it is like the blind leading the blind.
author: Sri M

text: Plato has said it brilliantly. He says ‘there are two eternal things in this universe– one ‘Is’ and is never becoming and the other ‘is not’ but is ever becoming’. That ‘becoming’ is what is known as ‘ jagat ‘. That movement – it is physical as well as psychological. For example, ‘I don’t have something, I must get it’ – a psychological movement. Physical – ‘I am in this location, I must move to that location’. The world is rotating all the time and also revolving around the geocentric system. So, that constant movement is called ‘ jagat '.
author: Sri M

text: ‘That which does not move’ – is that which is absolutely still like the eye of the cyclone, total motion but in the middle there is no movement – absolute calmness. And, it is from that calmness that everything is sucked in because it’s a vacuum. So that vacuum – ‘nothingness’ is very powerful.
author: Sri M

text: The world is such a funny place – you try to chase something and it always seems to run away from you…you leave it and it tries to follow you! It happens. Vishwamitra goes off to the forest for tapasya and Menaka follows him and dances for him! It is an amusing world. When you don’t want it, it comes to you!
author: Sri M

text: What I am saying is that there is nothing to fear. To live with this understanding is what is called holistic living. It is to live with the understanding that the entire universe is pervaded by that blissful Supreme Being and we are a part of that! This is not a fantasy that needs to be worked out in our minds. It is a fact and the actual process through which it is possible is known as sadhana or meditation.
author: Sri M

text: The Upanishad says that Supreme Truth or Reality is not a thing in the past – it is right Here and Now! Because it is right here, all our acquired knowledge cannot be applied to that Supreme Being. It is not something that you can study, store and remember. It is an immediate Presence here, available all the time!
author: Sri M

text: When the mind becomes quiet and silent, the aim of all forms of meditation – one comes face-to-face with one’s consciousness. This is a part of all human beings irrespective of caste, creed, religion or region.
author: Sri M

text: Experiencing life through the sorrows and the pleasures, the pains and the happiness that the body and the mind go through, one evolves into a better and cleaner entity before it touches a level that cannot even be called human, but divine.
author: Sri M

text: The human brain somehow seems to be wired for spiritual experience. Certain centers in the brain become active when you are in deep meditation. These are the centers thatyoga and Vedanta have talked about. In the present world, for the last hundred years or so, the cerebrum – part of the frontal lobe – has been over utilised while other parts of the brain are under-utilised and have not been developed.
author: Sri M

text: Through the practice of mysticism, whether it is Sufi, Yogic or Buddhist one, can awaken the centers that become active when you are in deep meditation. Only when these centers are awakened is there a possibility of looking into realms other than strictly material.
author: Sri M

text: Greed transfers itself even into the so-called spiritual system. I call this ‘spiritual materialism’. I don’t think real teachers are for sale. You can give a teacher millions of dollars. I don’t think he would teach someone who he thinks couldn’t be prepared for this.
author: Sri M

text: Outwardly we can bring about a response. We can help the poor to become better. All that is social work. But we believe that ultimately one would get the sense of equality only when there is a spiritual grounding, when one begins to understand that the divine spark is in you.
author: Sri M

text: Swami Vivekananda said, 'All the Gods that you see are only pictures created by people who don’t know, who have not seen them. But there are living Gods, human beings we can see face-to-face.' Serving a human being is the greatest form of worship. It also purifies your mind and prepares you for the spiritual journey.
author: Sri M

text: We say 'God created man in his own image'. Our idea is that, 'Man creates God in his own image.' For example – When you say ‘divine justice’, you automatically postulate a judge.
author: Sri M

text: When I wake up in the morning – the first thing that I recognise is that I exist. And then the world exists –I see everything around. But that first feeling that ‘I am’ –that awareness that ‘I am consciousness’ bereft of ‘I am this’ or ‘I am that’ –in its pure form is what we mean by the ‘atman’.
author: Sri M

text: Outwardly we can bring about a response. We can help the poor to become better. All that is social work. But we believe that ultimately one would get the sense of equality only when there is a spiritual grounding, when one begins to understand that the divine spark is in you.
author: Sri M

text: The sustainer and creator of the universe is the intelligent energy that permeates this universe. The ‘atman’, the consciousness that we understand, is a spark of that supreme consciousness. We cannot touch that supreme consciousness with our little individual minds.
author: Sri M

text: When the spark of individual consciousness merges with the universal, individuality is there but it is not a limited one. It is an individuality of universal consciousness. At no point does one become blank and lose one’s awareness. And, at no point, one feels that one has to work hard to be aware. One does not lose awareness.
author: Sri M

text: Sai Baba of Shirdi was a prime example of a manifestation of the Supreme Being in the form of a poor ‘Fakir’. To all intents and purposes, he looked like a poor Fakir, and yet, he taught the unity of not only Vedanta and the Hindu scriptures, but also pointed out that the Essential Reality of all humanity is One! This was the main message of Sai Baba.
author: Sri M

text: The message of Sai Baba of Shirdi was to convey the total unity of all religions. While living in a broken mosque, everyday he conducted the ritual of lighting a lamp or two there. Now, you know, nobody lights lamps in the evening in a mosque generally. He not only lit a lamp, but he said, ‘From now on, this broken down mosque will be called ‘Dwarka Mai’. Since then, the old mosque is called ‘Dwarka Mai’.
author: Sri M

text: You see affection is a great thing that links the Supreme Manifestation, or even a Teacher to those who can benefit from it. It is ‘affection,’ and it doesn’t ask for anything in return. It is an unexplained attraction. Nobody can say why. The rational intellect cannot explain this link.
author: Sri M

text: The message of Sai Baba of Shirdi was to convey the total unity of all religions. While living in a broken mosque, everyday he conducted the ritual of lighting a lamp or two there. Now, you know, nobody lights lamps in the evening in a mosque generally. He not only lit a lamp, but he said, ‘From now on, this broken down mosque will be called ‘Dwarka Mai’. Since then, the old mosque is called ‘Dwarka Mai’.
author: Sri M

text: Sai Baba of Shirdi would say ‘ Allah Malik Hai ,’ or ‘ Ram, Ram’ when people went to him with their problems. No one could say whether he was a Muslim, Hindu, or a Christian. His basic message was to unite, to bring people together, because Allah and Ram to Him were the same, though we call God by different names.
author: Sri M

text: Most of the benefits derived from Sai Baba were through Satsangs . The Satsang would sometimes be by touch, by talk,or by sight. He never taught people by talking about philosophy or the scriptures. He just talked to them about ordinary life. In every action and every experience his devotees had with him, he proved to them that he was not confined to the physical body – that the physical body that they saw was not ‘Baba’. The physical was the centre from which that Supreme Body was operating – that’s all!
author: Sri M

text: We think we can solve everything with our rational brain! This is one of the problems man faces when he reads the scriptures. He feels that with his intellect, he can explain everything. Now, one must understand that the intellect, however much it expands, has a limit beyond which it cannot go! And, the intelligent man is the one who realizes this. An intelligent man is one who realizes that his puny brain cannot understand many things.
author: Sri M

text: There’s a faculty that opens by which one can probably begin to understand these things. That is called the opening of the ‘Heart’. It is not open-heart surgery! We are not talking of an anatomical heart. It is the opening of the inner–faculty called the ‘ Hridaya Chakra’ in the scriptures. And, that opens through affection, compassion, love, devotion, and satsang .
author: Sri M

text: Satsang is critical – because you become according to the company you keep. If I live with people who talk about the Truth or want to find out what it is; who do japa and kirtan and bhajan , then I become like them in due course. It may take time. If I continue to live with people who are planning which drink to have next, I will become like that – it is but natural.
author: Sri M

text: Sai Baba was a strange person. Sometimes, his mood would be terrible, and nobody would dare go near him. And then, sometimes, he would be so affectionate that you could do anything – nothing mattered! You can’t gauge the mood of such Beings – like avadhootas, for instance.
author: Sri M

text: The central message is –there is only One Supreme Being and that Supreme Being resides in the hearts of all. He is the Antaryami . By living a good life, praying, meditating and trying to touch the Lotus Feet of this Being, who resides in your own heart, one can grow and attain great spiritual heights.
author: Sri M

text: Sai Baba always said, 'I give people what they ask – thinking, hoping, they will ask me one day what I really want to give them'. But, it is unfortunate that in this materialistic world, even when there is a treasure being offered to us in the form of spiritual communion with God, we don’t want that! We are more interested in our petty little things and ask only for things to keep us happy in this world.
author: Sri M

text: What each one of us must understand is to first lead a good life by helping as many people as possible, to sing the name of God, to do our ‘ japa ’, and to dwell on the Inner Spirit constantly. This inner spirit is the same who manifested as the Sai Baba of Shirdi. He may manifest today as one person, He may manifest tomorrow as another. The manifestation is different, but the Power behind it is the same.
author: Sri M

text: Sai Baba used to say that he practiced Guru Yoga , complete attention on the teacher. Baba would mention his Guru, a man called Venkusha who lived in the Nizam’s provinces in Andhra Pradesh, closer to Maharashtra. He was the zamindar of that province. In his youth, Baba lived with this person, Venkusha, for sometime and all the s adhana he did was to sit and look at His Guru wide-eyed and nothing else. He said that he looked and looked and looked! He also listened to what was taught to others.
author: Sri M

text: If we live for thirty-five or forty years close to someone who we consider a great teacher, like the Sai Baba of Shirdi, and worship him, but if our lives do not change as his teaching is meant to do and we remain as selfish as ever before, as angry as ever before, as petty as ever before – then it all comes to naught!
author: Sri M

text: Saburi means complete patience, especially in sadhana where one has to go through so many trials and tribulations. Sometimes, people take up sadhana very enthusiastically but the moment a little trouble comes upon them, they leave it. They run away because they think that either the problem has come because of the sadhana or they think, ‘let me put this right first, then I will go back to my meditation’. This never happens as sorrows, troubles, and tribulations are a part of our lives.
author: Sri M

text: Have patience in the face of criticism. Even when greatly agitated, try to be patient. Things will take care of themselves. We can never say when the Grace of God comes, so we cannot be impatient. Of course, we should be eager to get it. We should also wait patiently.
author: Sri M

text: Shraddha means absolute one-pointed attention. It has been translated as ‘Faith’ also. It actually means absolute, one-pointed attention; the complete attention on your goal.
author: Sri M

text: If both shraddha and saburi are there, then definitely, there is no problem in sadhana . What happens often is that: when there is shraddha, there is not enough saburi and the other way round. Both are necessary. Absolute, one-pointed total attention is required in our path along with infinite patience.
author: Sri M

text: While we practice our sadhana , if we sometimes get some powers, see lights or hear sounds – do not think that God is going to come! There are many people who have many powers, but have not yet had the darshan of the Lord. It is not the same; it could also be separate – there may be someone who shows no capacity for the so-called ‘s iddhis ’, but might have had the darshan of the Lord.
author: Sri M

text: So often, there may be a madman sitting in a corner, in the bus stand, or in the street somewhere, who may not show any powers, but he could very easily be an advanced, spiritual person. What I am trying to say is that one need not have any extra, fancy trimmings. Many of the avadhootas – like Gajanan Maharaj of Maharashtra, were all great saints.
author: Sri M

text: The insistence is on finding the truth – going towards the truth. That word, Truth is such an important word. So, in this pilgrimage of life too, stick to the truth as far as possible, especially on this journey because we live in a world where everything is a lie. Advertisements that we are exposed to in everyday life are lies, untruths or half-truths. This is the world we live in!
author: Sri M

text: At least in spiritual matters, please don’t lie! Don’t say I meditated for six hours today and lights were going up and down. Say only what you really feel. If you don’t follow this, it is the greatest blunder that can happen. We hear from people and read in books about something like this and we too imagine that we can see it. The mind plays tricks.
author: Sri M

text: Every day when you wake up in the morning, or go to bed at night, look at yourself and say, ‘where am I, what am I doing? How many falsities are still in my life? Am I really doing my sadhana sincerely?’ People say – I don’t have time. We have time for everything else. The fact is that urgency for sadhana has not arrived.
author: Sri M

text: In our relationship with the spiritual teacher – I won’t even use the word spiritual – in your relationship with the teacher, please be frank, truthful and clear. Don’t try to bluff, because it does not work. The teacher may not tell you so, but he knows and understands. So, be very frank.
author: Sri M

text: Spiritual development is not a mass affair. We cannot develop spiritually in groups. All that should be taken off from our minds. We are not sheep that can be herded together and made to eat the same food. Spiritual development is an individual affair.
author: Sri M

text: A clear understanding of anatomy and physiology is an important aspect of yoga. That is the first understanding of yourself. I am not saying you should all study medicine; you need not go into detail, just a general understanding of biology is all. If your consciousness were not linked to the physical organism, what is the use of all this? Through this, you will understand why yoga prescribes certain respiratory techniques, certain levels of breathing, certain rhythms and postures.
author: Sri M

text: The first step towards Self-realization is to understand the connection between the body and the brain, not just to keep repeating that I am the Supreme Brahman.
author: Sri M

text: In the ancient texts, anything that is described universally in the macrocosm will also be linked to something in the microcosm, the human system. The root of the Aswatha tree is the bottom of the spine in the human system while the top is the head and is called Kailas – where Mahadeva sits. The main trunk is the spinal cord. The nerves that radiate are the branches, the organs to which they go and operate are the leaves, and the different centers or a cluster where certain operations take place are the chakras .
author: Sri M

text: According to our parampara of Kriya, this whole system of the world is linked to the body. All pilgrimages are performed within, Kailash being on the top. When we do the parikrama , you should remember that you are also paying homage to Mahadeva , who sits within. So, therefore, you are carrying ‘That’ within you all the time. Give a little consideration to the sacredness you are carrying once in a while, and know you are not just a bundle of flesh and bones!
author: Sri M

text: I believe that Jesus was a great wandering teacher, with no house to live in. ‘The snakes have holes and foxes have dens, but the Son of Man does not know where to lay his head’- this is a statement from him, this wandering Yogi .
author: Sri M

text: We are either full of our own thoughts or we are full of our own prejudices. We are full of what others have taught us or what has been filled into our brain. There is no space; usually, there is no space at all! It is filled to the brim. And, if you are filled to the brim, how can you learn anything? It is not possible.
author: Sri M

text: When you say ‘empty yourself,’ it could also mean – ‘empty yourself of your prejudices.’ Empty yourself of all ideas that have been put into your brain, of all your preferences, of things that you instantly dislike and like because our sub-consciousness has been conditioned to certain things. Emptying all this is actually the process of Sadhana .
author: Sri M

text: Kriya simply means 'a method, practice, or technique'. We should understand there is no technique to find the Truth. It is not a feat of engineering. However, Kriya could help prepare the ground possibly, if we include other things too besides the practice.
author: Sri M

text: On this path to the Truth, we may think that we are denying ourselves many things. We are actually celebrating by leaving aside the little trinkets to find the big treasure.
author: Sri M

text: In this journey of understanding higher levels of consciousness, one has to be free of all burdens of the mind. This is where yoga comes in – to free the mind from the burdens.
author: Sri M

text: In the name of modern thinking and scientific enquiry, sadly some throw all traditions aside. Why discard something profound just because it is a tradition? You can adapt it. Discarding it is like throwing the baby out with the bathwater. That’s not intelligent or rational at all.
author: Sri M

text: According to the Rishis, Truth cannot be grasped and can only be understood by going as close as possible to it. The moment you think you have found it, it becomes something else. That continuously changing state introduces you to the gradual understanding of Truth. When it is finally understood, you become one with it.
author: Sri M

text: Humility is the understanding that one doesn’t know; or that, perhaps, there is more to know. The idea that one ‘knows’ has to be set aside, so that the mind is empty to receive.
author: Sri M

text: Though we may think we are human, in essence we are actually ‘pashus’ – animals. Shiva, who presides over us, is therefore called Pashupathi- Lord of the ‘pashus’.
author: Sri M

text: Of Shiva's armaments, one is the ‘paasha’ – noose. Shiva flings the noose only on those who are ready for it, and not at random. Believe me, being secured by this noose is beautiful.
author: Sri M

text: True consciousness is to transcend all images we create in our minds. The Tandav Nritya– 'primal dance of Shiva', is a beautiful expression for the annihilation of all images we have created.
author: Sri M

text: The Tandav Nritya of Shiva seeks to free you of all intrinsic conditioning that you are individual and different. If you are ready to embrace the Dancing Shiva, you are free!
author: Sri M

text: You cannot practice freedom because it has no preset design or pattern. Absolutely free and boundless - it cannot be ‘practiced’ in day-to-day life.
author: Sri M

text: Freedom is like the Wheel of Enlightenment - the rim symbolizes mindfulness while the hub stands for moral discipline; the veil of illusion is gradually lifted as one goes deeper into understanding one’s own self.
author: Sri M

text: Of the Trinity that creates, preserves and destroys, Shiva comes only at the end. Shiva, the Lord of the Universe is the ultimate destroyer. Kashi reminds you always that there is joy in destruction.
author: Sri M

text: In Sanskrit, 'Shivam' also means 'auspiciousness'. It also is a synonym for 'Ananda', 'happiness'. So, the contrast in Varanasi is that utter destruction is the same as auspiciousness and greatness.
author: Sri M

text: When everything is destroyed and one is left with no hope whatsoever, there comes Shiva’s support. As long as one remains attached to trivial things, the ultimate support - Shiva - cannot be found.
author: Sri M

text: Will somebody go to a teacher and say, “Break the images I have made of myself so that I can see what is real?” It is indeed terrible to break the images we have created in our minds. Shiva is the eternal symbol of the One who breaks.
author: Sri M

text: The reality of life includes violence, destruction, bloodshed, everything! You can hide but you cannot escape them. The moment you stand and face them, there is progress. Shiva is the perfect symbol of such progress.
author: Sri M

text: The best bhang is within us. This bhang helps us break all boundaries and remain in an ecstatic state - even in the midst of destruction.
author: Sri M

text: If you hope to achieve spiritual fulfillment after satisfying all material needs, then you live in a dream world! By the time you finish putting your house in order, it’s time to go to Manikarnika - the burning Ghat! This is the symbolism of Varanasi.
author: Sri M

text: The Ajna chakra is the Varanasi for the Yogi. Among the three nadis - the Sushumna, Ida, and the Pingala - Ajna is the place where the Ida and Pingala meet.
author: Sri M

text: One day - if you are lucky - while watching the river flowing, the boat sailing, and the sun rising, you will suddenly realize you are one with everything and not separate from the Kashi Viswanath who reigns in Varanasi.
author: Sri M

text: Rudra means 'destruction'. It also means, 'one who cries'. Rudra cries because there's so much pain in the world. Rudra is also the destroyer of pain. This is the reality of Varanasi and the Truth.
author: Sri M

text: Sit quietly and feel Viswanath in your heart or in the Ajna chakra. Sit quietly, allow the breeze to feel your ears, and chant Om.
author: Sri M

text: The word Guru means 'heavy' in Sanskrit. It also means 'teacher'. ‘Heavy’ - one who, by virtue of his knowledge, is a heavyweight. It also means 'one who destroys your ignorance'.
author: Sri M

text: Obsession conditions the mind; it doesn’t free the mind. When the mind is free, it finds its answer in a flash. The answer doesn’t come from heaven, it comes from within.
author: Sri M

text: Kriya simply means 'a method, practice, or technique'. We should understand there is no technique to find the Truth. It is not a feat of engineering. However, Kriya could help prepare the ground possibly, if we include other things too besides the practice.
author: Sri M

text: The Supreme Being is the link between all beings, worlds, and galaxies – like a thread holding the beads together in a rosary.
author: Sri M

text: In this journey of understanding higher levels of consciousness, one has to be free of all burdens of the mind. This is where yoga comes in – to free the mind from the burdens.
author: Sri M

text: The student or the listener must realize there are things to be learnt, of which he knows little and say: ‘Let me listen to somebody who seems to know’. This attitude curtails the egotistic feeling that comes in between when we listen.
author: Sri M

text: One thing that can be done is to sit down on New Year’s eve, take a piece of paper, and note down point-by-point – the characteristics and habits we find in ourselves that are negative and need to be overcome. Note them down and then, carefully, as you wake up to a new dawn, go through this again and begin to implement ways and means to get free of the negative tendencies. It can be done! The only way to get rid of negativity is to bring in positivity.
author: Sri M
